sentences.text: The ACT Integrity Commission investigated whether Education Directorate officials acted honestly and impartially during the 2019–2020 procurement for the Campbell Primary School Modernisation Project.
sentences.support:
into whether public officials in the ACT Education 
Directorate (EDU) failed to exercise their official functions honestly and or impartially

sentences.text: It examined the selection of Lendlease despite evaluation teams favouring Manteena, including communications involving ministerial staff, union officials and public servants.
sentences.support:
involved communications between the Minister’s office, 
union officials, persons within EDU and the Directorate tasked with delivery of the 
Project

sentences.text: The Commission found that the then director-general and the minister's chief of staff engaged in serious corrupt conduct by improperly influencing the procurement and trying to conceal what occurred.
sentences.support:
Accordingly, the corrupt conduct of each 
amounted to serious corrupt conduct.

sentences.text: The Commission declined to find that another official engaged in serious corrupt conduct, taking account of his later disclosures and efforts to correct the wrongdoing.
sentences.support:
I have concluded 
that it is not appropriate to find that Mr Green’s conduct, considered as a whole, 
amounted to serious corrupt conduct.

notes: No dedicated executive summary, overview or summary of findings was identified. The Introduction establishes the scope; the concluding findings are under “Was there corrupt conduct?” and “Serious corrupt conduct”. No Commission recommendations list was identified: the recommendations reproduced on PDF pages 293 and 296 belong to a probity audit. Existing OPAX findings are not duplicated. The official whose later disclosures were taken into account is not named in the summary.
